reason: 'They' in the context are the leaflets of the pinnate leaf. 'Sessile (or nearly so)' is rightly read as sessile with an 'approximately' qualifier.
18-23 lateral veins on each side of the midrib. The count, the each-side position and the midrib landmark (leaf midvein, PO_0020139) are all right.
The context is about the sepals: 'apex green to purple, rounded to acute'. The sepal apex grades from rounded (obtuse) to acute.
The leaf sheath is green or brownish (brown). The 'of proximal leaves' position is left out, but that does not make the statement false.

The leaves are glabrous or have a few scattered hairs. 'Pubescent hair' (PATO_0001320) is the project's standard class for pubescent. The words 'few scattered' and 'white' are left out but nothing is wrong.

The leaf margin is serrate-crenate, between serrate and crenate. Margin shapes put on the leaf lamina are the usual pattern here.

fix: Here 'en dessous' means 'in the lower part' of a stem, set against 'dans la zone inflorescentielle'. It does not mean the underside (abaxial), as it does for leaves.
reason: 'Cannelée' (fluted) means furrowed. The stem is grooved below and furrowed in the inflorescence zone, so 'stem furrowed' holds even without a position.

target: fruit with position 'base': obtuse (PATO_0001935) | abruptly narrowed (FLOPO_0991316)

reason: The fruit as a whole is subglobose or obovoid. Only its base is rounded or narrowed into a stipe, so the annotation is false without the base position.

fix: In 'calyx tube X', the part is the calyx tube, not the calyx.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on the petiole, colour yellow/golden, when young; and petiole villous when young
fix: In '<colour> villous/pubescent/tomentose', the colour belongs to the hairs, not to the organ that carries them.

target: higher order inflorescence axis / inflorescence branch (PO_0009081), lowest

target: stipule adnate (FLOPO_0991129) to petiole, with no frequency qualifier (or extent 'for most of its length')
fix: In 'mostly adnate to', 'mostly' tells how much of the stipule is joined (most of its length). It does not mean 'usually'.
reason: Rosa stipules are always joined to the petiole for most of their length. The 'usually' qualifier wrongly suggests they are sometimes free.

fix: In Meliaceae, 'staminal tube' is a part in its own right. It should not be grounded to 'stamen'.

fix: 'Stem leaves' should be grounded to cauline leaf, not to leaf. This matters most when the flora also describes other leaves, such as basal or caudex leaves.

The leaflets are elliptic-lanceolate. Reading this as a continuum between elliptic and lanceolate is right.

fix: 'Cunéé à obtus' is a range. The obtuse end should be kept as well, in a value relation.

The upper side of the leaf is pilose. 'Sparsely' and 'stellate' are left out, but nothing is false.
There are 1-4 seeds in each locule, and the locule (PO_0025263) is given as the container.
The fruit (a capsule) is elliptic.
